name: Verona Villafranca Valerio Catullo Airport
before:
Verona's airport, 10 km south west of the city at the junction of the A4 from Milan to Venice and the A22 up to the Brenner Pass. It draws from a population of more than four million across Verona, Brescia, Mantua, Trentino and South Tyrol.

Lake Garda is the reason many clients use it. From June to September ATV buses 164, 183 and 184 run hourly from the airport to the towns along the lake. Year round, the Aerobus shuttle connects to Verona Porta Nuova station.

The airport has an unusual piece of equipment. A fog dispersal system has been running since 2003, and together with an ILS Category IIIb approach it lets aircraft land in visibility as low as 75 metres.

Departures and arrivals are in two buildings side by side, with the bus stand directly outside arrivals.

The site was established in 1916 as a military airfield and only began civil flying in 1961.
after:
Verona's airport, 10 km south west of the city.

Lake Garda is the reason many clients use it. ATV's line 482 runs hourly from the airport to Peschiera and San Benedetto on the lake in season (until 18 October in 2026), with line 483 on to Lazise, Bardolino, Garda and Malcesine. Year round, ATV's Verona Airlink shuttle reaches Verona Porta Nuova station in 15 minutes and runs every 20 minutes.

The site began as a military airfield and started civil flying in 1961.
